html:
The Baška tablet is a stone slab carved around 1100 in the Glagolitic script, found in the small church of Saint Lucy near Baška on the island of Krk in Croatia.

It records a gift of land by King Zvonimir to the abbey, and it is the first known text to name a Croatian king in the Croatian language. Croatian priests kept the Glagolitic alphabet, created by Saints Cyril and Methodius, longer than anyone else, and Rome allowed them to say Mass in Slavonic. The tablet is called the baptism certificate of the Croatian nation, and it is now kept in Zagreb. Krk was a centre of this tradition, linked to the medieval kingdom.
sum: The Baška tablet is a stone slab carved around 1100 in the Glagolitic script, found in the small church of Saint Lucy near Baška on the island of Krk in Croatia.
